SECRET

H. B. M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.
1st. November, 1929.

My dear Aiers,

With reference to your letter No.
D.528 dated the 7th. of October, 1929, on the subject
of the suspected Communist C.P.Headley, I have received
a further telegram from India regarding this individual
which makes it clear that his name should have been spelt
Leadley. His description is given as: age about thirty
or thirty-five years, tall, slim and clean shaven but
India has no further information about him. The name
was communicated to me purely on the off chance of his
having been in China and of our having some information
about him on record.

Does the change of name and description
now given help you in tracing any such person?

Yours sincerely,

C. H. K. Hall.

R. C. Aiers, Esq.,
Assistant Commissioner of Police,
Criminal Investigation Department,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

Foreign Section,
For inquiry and report please
JLS 2/11/29

机密

英国驻上海总领事馆，
上海。
1929年11月1日。

亲爱的 Aiers：

关于您1929年10月7日第 D.528 号信函，涉及涉嫌共产主义者 C.P. Headley 一事，我收到来自印度关于此人的进一步电报，明确指出其姓名拼写应为 Leadley。对其体貌特征的描述为：年龄约三十至三十五岁，身材高大、瘦削、面部无须，但印度方面没有关于他的更多资料。提供该姓名纯属碰运气，指望他可能曾在中国，且我们存档中有关于他的某些信息。

现提供的姓名变更及体貌特征描述，是否有助于您追查此人？

此致

敬礼

C. H. K. Hall。

R. C. Aiers 先生，
助理警务总监，
刑事侦缉处，
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。

外侨股，
请调查并报告
JLS 29年11月2日

October 7 29.

Dear Colonel,

With reference to your letter of September 24,
I have to state that no trace can be found of C.P. Headley,
and there is nothing in the records of the Municipal Police
to show that a person bearing that name has been connected
in any way with Communist activities.

I shall be thankful if you will kindly when answering
the communication you have received point out to the Indian
Authorities the advisability, when addressing such inquiries
to Shanghai, of forwarding all the information they possess
regarding the persons about whom the inquiries are made.
In consequence of a lack of surveillance over persons
entering and leaving China, undesirables are able to use
false names with impunity and they frequently resort to this
subterfuge in order to avoid attracting attention to their
presence here.

Yours sincerely,
Sca.

Lieut. Col. G.H.R. Halland, O.B.E.,
H.B.M. Consulate.

29年10月8日
1929年10月7日。

亲爱的上校：

关于您9月24日的来信，我必须指出，查无 C.P. Headley 的踪迹，工部局警务处的档案中也没有任何记录显示有以此命名的人与共产主义活动有任何关联。

如果您在回复所收到的来函时，能向印度当局指出，在向上海发出此类查询时，宜将其掌握的关于被查询人员的所有信息一并 forwarded（转发），我将不胜感激。由于对进出中国的人员缺乏监控，不受欢迎分子能够肆无忌惮地使用假名，他们经常采用这种诡计以避免引起人们对其在此地存在的注意。

此致

敬礼

Sca.

G.H.R. Halland 中校，O.B.E.勋衔，
英国驻华领事馆。

24th September, 1929.

My dear Aiers,

A European Communist named C.P. HEADLEY has
appeared in India, and I have been asked whether I know
anything about him, from which I presume that HEADLEY
arrived in India from the Far East. Would you kindly
let me know whether you have ever heard of such an indiv-
idual.

Yours sincerely,
C.H.N. Hall.

R.C. Aiers Esquire,
Director of Criminal Intelligence,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

528。
29年9月24日。
上海
1929年9月24日。

亲爱的 Aiers：

一名名为 C.P. HEADLEY 的欧洲共产主义者在印度出现，有人询问我是否了解他的情况，据此我推测 HEADLEY 是从远东抵达印度的。能否请您告知我，您是否曾听说过此人。

此致

敬礼

C.H.N. Hall。

R.C. Aiers 先生，
刑事情报处处长，
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。
